artifact.hint: Leonardo da Vinci's portrait vanished from the Louvre with its provenance card, shipping sleeve, and conservation notes.

pattern.label: Renaissance provenance route
pattern.summary: The thief is laundering the painting through places tied to Renaissance art, museum catalogues, and old European collection routes.

clues.title: Baggage direction
clues.text: A private crate left Paris for a European country southeast of the Louvre. The handler remembered a destination tied to Leonardo, not to a modern auction house.

clues.title: Renaissance catalogue card
clues.text: The torn catalogue card references Renaissance workshop records and portrait studies, pointing toward the country most directly associated with Leonardo's early career.

clues.title: Trade packing
clues.text: The crate padding used a wine merchant's sleeve and clothing-house inventory paper. It looks like cover cargo from a country known for wine and fashion exports.

clues.title: Romance-language permit
clues.text: The permit translation stayed inside the Romance-language corridor, but the seal did not match France, Spain, or Portugal. ACME flags Italy as the cleanest fit.

clues.title: Conservator request
clues.text: A guest asked for a late train to a city with portrait conservation labs and Renaissance archives. The city name was not written down, but the question sounded like Florence.

followups.text: Back in Paris, the Louvre archivist confirms the missing shelf mark belonged to a Florence loan file, not a Paris exhibition file.

clues.title: Northern studio note
clues.text: The Uffizi archive ledger mentions a northern European restoration studio famous for canal freight and old-master trade records.

clues.title: Solvent invoice
clues.text: A solvent invoice was bundled with machinery and pharmaceutical export paperwork, a better fit for the Netherlands than the Mediterranean decoys.

clues.title: Northwest transfer
clues.text: The next crate moved northwest from Italy, still inside Europe, toward a low-lying country with a major capital-area airport.

clues.title: Canal booking
clues.text: The thief asked for a hotel near canals and a restoration studio, then corrected the clerk when he suggested Venice.

clues.title: Low-country seal
clues.text: The diplomatic pouch number points to the Low Countries, but the language mark is not Belgian. That leaves the Dutch file brightest on ACME's board.

followups.text: The Florence clerk remembers the thief rejecting Venice because the next stop had canals and northern old-master dealers, not Italian Renaissance galleries.

clues.title: Royal collection trail
clues.text: The altered provenance page points to a royal collection city with deep Habsburg-era paperwork and major European museum records.

clues.title: Mediterranean cargo relabel
clues.text: The fake cargo relabel lists wine, vehicles, and Mediterranean food shipments. It is too southern for the Low Countries and too western for Italy.

clues.title: Southwest sleeve
clues.text: The cargo sleeve shows a southwest route inside Europe, toward a capital whose name starts with M.

clues.title: Museum nickname
clues.text: A courier kept saying 'the meadow file' in bad translation. ACME thinks that is a clumsy hint at the Prado.

clues.title: Spanish seal
clues.text: The replacement export seal is Spanish, but the stated artwork origin is false. That contradiction is strong enough for a warrant in Madrid.

deadEnds.default: The field office found no match for the cultural pattern. At least one strong clue contradicts this destination.
deadEnds.France: The trail began in France, but the collected evidence points away from the Louvre after the theft.
deadEnds.Portugal: Portugal fits part of the Romance-language trail, but the Renaissance and export evidence do not support it.
deadEnds.Belgium: Belgium fits the Low Countries clue, but the language and canal-restoration evidence point farther north.
deadEnds.Italy: Italy is already part of the route. For this leg, the later evidence points beyond the Renaissance archive.
